statements.venue: Press conference with Reps. Beyer, Lieu and Trahan (remarks published as press release)
statements.quote: The race with China isn’t only about who can build the most advanced model first. Getting to the best system first doesn’t matter if people don’t use it or if AI has killed all of us in the meantime.
statements.context: Calling on Speaker Johnson to cancel recess and pass AI safety legislation, arguing regulation does not mean losing to China.
statements.reason: She names AI killing all of us as a possible outcome, which is extinction framing, though it is phrased as a rhetorical aside rather than a direct claim.

statements.venue: Press conference with Reps. Beyer, Lieu and Trahan (remarks published as press release)
statements.quote: And it can hurt people – in small everyday ways, and in catastrophic ones.
statements.context: Opening of the same remarks, on what a decade of working on AI has taught her.
statements.reason: States in her own words that AI can cause catastrophic harm, not limited to misuse, but without naming the harm (between B and C).

statements.venue: Letter to Secretary of State Rubio and Treasury Secretary Bessent, led by Jacobs, Meeks and Bera with 26 other Democrats
statements.quote: Last week, researchers from Anthropic and Open AI — America’s top two AI labs — warned the world that the technology is hurtling toward a future that, minus guardrails, could endanger humanity.
statements.context: Letter urging a sustained US-China dialogue on AI safety risks, including shared red lines and a crisis channel.
statements.source_label: Rep. Sara Jacobs press release (letter excerpt)
statements.reason: Relays a warning that AI could endanger humanity and uses it as the basis for the letter's call to act (ruling 2); endorsement is by the letter's request rather than explicit words, so marked boundary.

statements.venue: Letter to Secretary of State Rubio and Treasury Secretary Bessent, led by Jacobs, Meeks and Bera with 26 other Democrats
statements.quote: AI models could be used to create a deadly pathogen, carry out a cyberattack on critical infrastructure, or destabilize societies in other ways.
statements.context: Same letter, describing the national security risks of AI.
statements.source_label: Rep. Sara Jacobs press release (letter excerpt)
statements.reason: Names catastrophic harm (a deadly pathogen) only as misuse of AI by people, which is C under the 11 November ruling.

statements.quote: A lot of what we’re seeing right now is in the testing phases, is these AI agents not following the rules they were given or finding to deceive the companies in the role … these sort of tasks that they’ve been given to do in this testing environment.
statements.context: Article on AI industry figures warning of extinction risk; directly preceded by her words "I think the risks are very real" in a separate quoted piece.
statements.reason: Says the risks are very real and points to AI agents breaking rules and deceiving developers, but names no catastrophic consequence herself (ruling 4).

statements.venue: Press release introducing the ATOMIC Act with Rep. Celeste Maloy
statements.quote: As AI becomes more powerful, we have a responsibility to identify and guard against new risks before they become real-world threats. That’s why I’m proud to co-lead the bipartisan ATOMIC Act to identify AI-related nuclear risks, establish safeguards, and develop mitigation plans.
statements.context: Bill directing Energy Department national labs to test the most advanced AI systems for nuclear-related risks, including deceptive behavior and bypassing safety guardrails.
statements.reason: Acknowledges serious nuclear-related risks from more powerful AI in general terms without stating a catastrophic outcome.

statements.venue: Press release introducing the Human Authority over Autonomous Weapons Act with Reps. Beyer and Barrett
statements.quote: AI mistakes on the battlefield have the potential to be catastrophic: civilian casualties, friendly fire, unintended escalation, and calculations made on faulty data,
statements.context: Bill requiring a human in the loop before AI-enabled weapons use lethal force.
statements.reason: About military use of AI, which is D under ruling 3 despite the word catastrophic.

statements.venue: Press release on the SAFE AI Act outline
statements.quote: Right now, the companies write their own rules while their own models break out of test environments and hack other companies’ systems. Americans are rightly concerned about unchecked AI threatening public safety, critical infrastructure, national security, and the systems we all depend on.
statements.context: Jacobs co-leads the forthcoming SAFE AI Act, which she says includes emergency authority to stop dangerous models posing a serious and immediate danger.
statements.source_label: Office of Rep. Beyer press release, 2026-11-19
statements.reason: Names AI systems acting on their own (escaping test environments) as a threat to public safety and national security, a serious but general threat, which ruling 4 places at C.

slowdown.note: No statement found on slowing frontier AI progress; she argues guardrails, not speed, win the race with China.

pause.note: No statement found on pausing frontier AI.

grade_reason: In September 2026 she said that winning the AI race does not matter "if AI has killed all of us in the meantime", and led a letter relaying a warning that AI could endanger humanity; both are 2026 and no dismissive statement was found. Both A statements are boundary cases (one rhetorical, one relayed), so B is the fallback if a reviewer reads them strictly.
